terms.meaning: "Re-birth" or "revival": the burst of new literature, art and science in Europe, about 1400-1600 C.E., starting in Italy.
The belief that man plays the main role in the world and is God's greatest creation, not a sinner.
Testing every idea by reason, without prejudice, and accepting it only if true.
"One who rebelled": the Catholic Church's name for Luther's followers.
The Catholic Church's effort to reform itself from within.
One country's political and economic control over another's territory.

items.name: Three ages of European history
items.formula: Ancient: till about 500 C.E. Middle: about 500 to 1500 C.E. Modern: from about 1500 C.E.
items.example: Renaissance, Reformation and Explorations mark the modern age.

items.name: Fall of Constantinople
items.formula: Turkish Sultan Mohammed II took it in 1453 C.E.; its scholars fled to Italy with Greek and Latin books.

items.name: Printing press
items.formula: Gutenberg used movable type at Mainz around 1450 C.E.; Caxton set up a press in England in 1477.
items.example: One person could print 24,000 copies a year instead of two books.

items.name: Renaissance writers
items.formula: Petrarch (sonnets), Dante (Divine Comedy), Boccaccio (Decameron), Cervantes (Don Quixote).
items.example: Shakespeare: Julius Caesar, Romeo and Juliet, King Lear, Macbeth.

items.name: Renaissance art
items.formula: Leonardo da Vinci: Mona Lisa, The Last Supper, Virgin on the Rocks. Michael Angelo: statue of Moses. Donatello: David.
items.example: Churches: St. Peter's in Rome, St. Paul's in London, with round arches.

items.name: Renaissance science
items.formula: Copernicus: the Earth goes round the Sun. Kepler proved him right. Galileo made the telescope.
items.example: Newton explained gravity; Harvey found blood circulation.

items.name: Early reformers
items.formula: John Wycliffe, the "Morning Star of the Reformation", at Oxford.
items.example: John Hus refused to act against his conscience and was burnt alive.

items.name: Martin Luther
items.formula: Opposed Pope Leo X's sale of indulgences; nailed 95 statements on the Wittenberg church door.
items.example: He translated the Bible into German.

items.name: Ignatius Loyola
items.formula: A Spanish general who led the Counter Reformation and founded the Society of Jesus in 1541 C.E.
items.example: Its members, the Jesuits, spread education and health care.

items.name: Causes of the explorations
items.formula: Turks blocked trade at Constantinople; Marco Polo's reports of rich Asia; demand for spices.
items.example: Compass, astrolabe and caravel ships made long voyages possible.

items.name: Prince Henry and Bartholomeo Diaz
items.formula: Henry the Navigator founded a navigation school. Diaz reached Africa's southern tip in 1488.
items.example: Diaz called it the Cape of Storms; King John II renamed it the Cape of Good Hope.

items.name: Vasco da Gama
items.formula: Reached Calicut on India's west coast in 1498, via the Cape of Good Hope and Melindi.
items.example: He actually landed at Kappad, about 10 km from Calicut, ruled by the Zamorins.

items.name: Christopher Columbus
items.formula: Sailed west for Spain in August 1492 with 88 sailors; sighted land on 12 October 1492.
items.example: He reached the Bahamas (West Indies), thought it was India and called the people Red Indians.

items.name: Brazil and the name America
items.formula: Cabral reached Brazil by accident. Amerigo Vespucci called the land a New World.
items.example: Geographer Waldseemüller named it America after Amerigo.

items.name: Ferdinand Magellan
items.formula: Left Spain in 1519 with 5 ships; crossed the Magellan Strait into the calm Pacific; killed in the Philippines.
items.example: His ship Victoria returned in 1522: the first round-the-world voyage.

items.name: Effects of the explorations
items.formula: Global trade grew, Christianity spread, and Europeans competed for colonies.
items.example: The cruel slave trade began in the West Indies, Mexico, Peru and Brazil.

mistakes.text: Order of voyages: Diaz 1488, Columbus 1492, Vasco da Gama 1498, Magellan 1519-1522.
Magellan himself died in the Philippines; his crew finished the voyage on the Victoria.
Columbus never reached India: he reached the West Indies and didn't know it was a new land.
